Package de.hof.dms.controller

Class AdminDepartmentController

java.lang.Object
de.hof.dms.controller.AdminDepartmentController
@RestController @RequestMapping("/api/admin") @Profile("!no-mongo") public class AdminDepartmentController extends Object
Admin REST endpoints for the department registry and for assigning departments to users, under /api/admin.

Access is restricted to users with the dms_admin realm role via the URL-based authorization rules in SecurityConfig. Only active when a MongoDB backend is present (profile !no-mongo).

    • list

      @GetMapping("/departments") public List<DepartmentResponse> list()
      Lists all departments in the registry, ordered by code.
      Returns:
      the department list

    • create

      @PostMapping("/departments") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<DepartmentResponse> create(@RequestBody CreateDepartmentRequest request)
      Creates a new department, returning HTTP 201 on success. The code is normalized and must be unique.
      Parameters:
      request - the creation payload (code, optional display name)
      Returns:
      a 201 response containing the created department

    • update

      @PutMapping("/departments/{code}") public DepartmentResponse update(@PathVariable("code") String code, @RequestBody UpdateDepartmentRequest request)
      Updates a department's display name and/or active flag. The code itself is immutable.
      Parameters:
      code - the department code from the path
      request - the fields to change (nulls keep current values)
      Returns:
      the updated department

    • delete

      @DeleteMapping("/departments/{code}") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<Void> delete(@PathVariable("code") String code)
      Deletes a department that is no longer referenced by users, folders, documents, or ACLs; otherwise responds 409 (deactivate instead).
      Parameters:
      code - the department code from the path
      Returns:
      a 204 response on success

    • assignUserDepartment

      @PutMapping("/users/{userId}/department") public org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<Void> assignUserDepartment(@PathVariable("userId") String userId, @RequestBody AssignDepartmentRequest request)
      Assigns a department to a Keycloak user or removes the assignment (blank department). Only existing, active departments may be assigned; the change is written to the user's Keycloak department attribute.
      Parameters:
      userId - the Keycloak user id from the path
      request - the assignment payload
      Returns:
      a 204 response on success
